summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old male with a history of COPD, interstitial lung disease, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, lung cancer after radiation therapy, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for a three-day history of worsening shortness of breath, dry cough, and orthopnea. He denied fever, chest pain radiation, or lower extremity edema. Initial evaluation showed elevated BNP and chronic interstitial lung changes on imaging without acute pulmonary edema. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with azithromycin, prednisone, and nebulizer treatments, leading to rapid improvement in respiratory status. His blood glucose was elevated, prompting a temporary adjustment in insulin regimen with increased glargine doses. He remained stable, ambulated independently, and was discharged home after two days with a plan to complete antibiotics and steroids, resume baseline medications, and follow up with pulmonology, primary care, and cardiology. Tobacco cessation support was encouraged.
